architecture.mechanism: Classification of subjects into high- and low-productivity groups based on a quantitative energy threshold (greater than 75 MJ/d versus less than 75 MJ/d) enables detection of sub-populations whose performance diverges once an energy budget is exceeded.
architecture.intervention: Install a quantitative thermal-energy threshold check in the 2020 Honda Civic thermal management ECU: classify each driving cycle as either above or below a defined cooling-load threshold (analogous to the 75 MJ/d cutoff), and when a cycle exceeds the threshold, trigger an additional diagnostic branch that cross-checks electric power steering load, coolant temperature, and fuel-system vapor pressure to isolate whether overheating, steering torque anomalies, and fuel odor are co-occurring symptoms of the same root cause.
architecture.expected_effect: Intermittent co-occurrence of steering pull, coolant overheating, and fuel odor under sustained high thermal load (e.g., ~65 mph highway driving) will be captured as a single correlated failure mode rather than as three independent intermittent faults, enabling targeted repair of the shared thermal/electrical pathway.
architecture.falsification_test: Recreate the failure on a dynamometer by holding 65 mph equivalent load for 30+ minutes while logging coolant temperature, EPS motor current/torque, and fuel-tank pressure sensor voltage; if the steering and odor events do not cluster within a defined thermal-load window above the set threshold, the energy-threshold classification hypothesis is falsified.
